newsitem.title: DUBAI: TENNIS-INJURED BECKER PULLS OUT OF DUBAI OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-INJURED BECKER PULLS OUT OF DUBAI OPEN.

text.p: A recurring wrist injury forced Boris Becker to pull out of the $1 million Dubai Tennis Open on Friday, just minutes before a scheduled quarter-final against Goran Ivanisevic.
"How serious the injury is I cannot tell at the moment, but the pain is so severe I can't even open my wallet," he said.
Becker, who withdrew from last year's Wimbledon after tearing a tendon in his right wrist, added: "There is no sense in playing when I can't even open a bottle of water.
"I felt fine at the end of last year and in the Australian Open, so I'm surprised I have the pain right now.
"I don't know when I will be able to play my next tournament. The injury would usually heal after a couple of days' practice, but this time it has got worse."

With the German's exit, top seed Ivanisevic moved unchallenged into the semifinals where he was joined by Jim Courier, who produced another impeccable performance to earn the scalp of fourth seed Wayne Ferreira, in straight sets 6-2 7-5.

The former number one, now ranked 22 in the world, produced an array of superb groundstrkes mixed with delicate lobs, to frustrate a surprisingly out-of-sorts South African, the winner of the 1995 Dubai Open event.
"It's a nice feeling to play well after travelling half the planet to reach Dubai," said Courier, who had just two days of rest following Davis Cup duty in Brazil.
In another quarter-final, unseeded Jiri Novak continued his fine run of success with an effortless 6-2 6-2 victory over Wimbledon champion and third seed Richard Krajicek.
The Czech player, who defeated Australian Open finalist Carlos Moya in the first round, led 3-0 and then 5-2 before wrapping up the set with another break.
The Dutchman's miserable day was typified in the second set by an overhead he attempted which landed on his side of the net, resulting in Krajicek hurling his racket to the ground in frustration.
